rounds.text: Nagarjuna Agri Tech Ltd trades at an alarming P/E of 83.8 [E1], which balloons to 121.59x when measured against a sector benchmark of just 19.15x [E6]. This excessive valuation is entirely divorced from the company's fundamentals, as demonstrated by a miserable return on assets of 0.22% compared to the sector benchmark of 3.52% [E8]. Furthermore, the EV/EBITDA multiple stands at an inflated 49.62x against a sector benchmark of 11.88x [E11], while providing zero dividend yield to shareholders [E4]. Independent valuation modeling shows that a discounted cash flow intrinsic value sits at a mere Rs 21 per share against a market price of Rs 47 [E43], resulting in a negative margin of safety of -125.0% [E44]. To justify today's price, the company must deliver an unrealistic 29.3% earnings growth, vastly outstripping the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E45], while past performance already shows the stock running aggressively ahead of fundamentals with a 50% price growth outpacing a 24% profit growth over five years [E54]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio is 0.94x [E2], trading slightly below the sector benchmark of 1.79x [E7].
